requirement_threshold: Association must maintain official records within the state and in an organized manner facilitating owner inspection.
Records must be made available after written request to the board or its designee.
Failure to produce within 10 working days creates presumption of willful noncompliance.
retention_deadline: $50 per calendar day, up to 10 days, beginning 11th working day

requirement_threshold: Association must simultaneously provide a checklist of records made available and records withheld.
Associations with 150+ units (no timeshare units) must post certain documents online.
Associations managing a condominium with 25+ units (no timeshare units) must post certain documents online.
Must be retained as part of accounting records.
retention_deadline: At least 15 years after study completion

requirement_threshold: Copy of inspection report must be retained by the association.
Contracts for work to be performed, including bids.
Ballots, sign-in sheets, voting proxies and related papers.
retention_deadline: 1 year from date of election, vote, or meeting

requirement_threshold: Plans/permits/warranties, declaration, bylaws, articles of incorporation, current rules, and meeting minutes.
Director, board member, or CAM who knowingly, willfully, and repeatedly violates records law commits a 2nd degree misdemeanor and must be removed from office.
Destroying official records in furtherance of a crime is punishable as evidence tampering or obstruction of justice.
Owners generally must file a petition for alternative dispute resolution before a records dispute is heard by a court.
retention_deadline: Appeal within 30 days of arbitrator's final order

requirement_threshold: Stricter inspection and HOA budgeting rules, particularly for condos three stories or higher.
